spans.s:
Ropaṇākā is the name of a bird mentioned in the Rigveda and the Atharvaveda. The ‘thrush’ seems to be meant; but Keśava, the commentator on the kauśika sūtra, is inclined to understand the word to mean a sort of wood.
Foot notes i. 50, 12.
i. 22, 4. Cf. taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 7, 6, 22.
Śārikā, Sāyaṇa on Rv., loc. cit. On Av. i. 22, 4, he explains it as kāṣṭhaśuka, perhaps a kind of parrot.
xxvi. 20.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 92; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 266; Caland, Altindisches Zauberritual, 76, n. 13; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 23.
